title: Bangkok, 10 December 1968
hook: he died in an accident, twenty-seven years to the day after entering the monastery

segments.voice: Yesterday, Polonnaruwa: barefoot before the great stone figures, a moment of clear seeing. Your line was seeing clearly. About a week later, Merton was in Bangkok.

Some dates line up in a way nobody could plan. On December 10, 1941, a young man rang the bell at the gate of Gethsemani and asked to become a monk. On December 10, 1968, that same man, now fifty-three and famous, gave a morning talk to a gathering of monks and nuns near Bangkok, went back to his room after lunch, and never came out. Twenty-seven years to the day. Today is gentle, about an ending.
screen: `DECEMBER 10, 1941: THE GATE.` → `DECEMBER 10, 1968: BANGKOK.` → `TWENTY-SEVEN YEARS TO THE DAY.`

segments.voice: First, the conference. Merton had come to Asia partly to speak at a meeting of Catholic monks and nuns from across the continent, at a retreat center outside Bangkok. That morning he gave his talk, on monastic life and the modern world. At the end he said they'd take questions later and, lightly, that for now he'd disappear. Second, the accident. After lunch he went to rest. He had taken a shower, and later that afternoon he was found dead, a faulty electric fan fallen across him. The most accepted account is that he was electrocuted. Some questions about the details have been raised since, and the sources don't settle all of them. Third, the journey home. His body was flown back to the United States on a military plane, alongside the bodies of American soldiers killed in Vietnam. The monk who had written so much against war went home with its dead. He was buried at Gethsemani, in the monks' cemetery, under a plain white cross like his brothers. Fourth, the day he began. Catholics don't treat a sudden death as meaningless or as punishment. Jesus said, in the Douay-Rheims: "Watch ye therefore, because you know not the day nor the hour." Not a threat, but an invitation to live each day awake. And the Church prays for those who die suddenly, trusting the words at every Catholic funeral: "I am the resurrection and the life." Merton's end came on the anniversary of his beginning. Many who loved him read it as a quiet sign: the monk had finished his road.
screen: `A MORNING TALK NEAR BANGKOK.` · `AN ACCIDENT IN THE AFTERNOON.` · `HOME WITH THE WAR'S DEAD.` · `YOU KNOW NOT THE DAY NOR THE HOUR.` · then, large: `I AM THE RESURRECTION AND THE LIFE.`

segments.voice: Let one person come to mind who died suddenly, someone you knew or someone in the news, who left with no goodbye. You don't have to relive how it happened; just hold them gently and remember one good thing about them. If you pray, pray for them and for the people who miss them, as Catholics pray for the dead every day, especially at Mass.
Bangkok. Where Thomas Merton died in an accident on December 10, 1968, twenty-seven years to the day after he entered Gethsemani. Today's word.
Your line: the day he began. The week's lines: the desire counts, a small house in the woods, silence that speaks, friendship without erasing, alone for them, seeing clearly. That's the week.

howItsDone: Catholics pray for the dead at every Mass and especially in November, and when someone dies suddenly, families often ask a priest to offer a Mass for them.

Death: 10 December 1968 at the Red Cross conference center in Samut Prakan near Bangkok, during the AIM meeting of Asian monastic superiors; apparent electrocution by a faulty fan after a shower. Later writers (e.g. a 2018 book) have questioned the investigation; the script says only that questions have been raised and sources don't settle all of them. Confirm tone.
His remark that he would 'disappear' is paraphrased, not quoted.
Body flown home on a U.S. military aircraft with the bodies of soldiers killed in Vietnam; buried at Gethsemani on 17 December 1968. Confirm.
